evidence: Persistent bottle-within-arm differences explain 1% (BRL) and 15% (LBE) of ln-yield variance; control bottle IV.3 failed while its replicates did not.
No feedstock, pyrolysis temperature, surface area, conductivity or particle size for the Sanglier biochar is committed; one material only, so no descriptor effect is estimable inside the study.
BRL reactor mass is not recorded; temperature is not a committed field; trace-element regimes differ by lab (High vs Low).
Batch (substrate lot / cycle) explains 64% (BRL) and 38% (LBE) of ln-yield variance versus 15% and 12% for arm.

Only 1.2% of admitted cycles meet the 1%/day stop rule (median final-day increment 8% of cumulative), yet full-cycle Gompertz fits place the asymptote only 5.5% above the last observation. A single-pool curve per cycle also ignores carry-over biomass and residual substrate. No alternative structure was tested, so this stays unproven.

Gompertz fitted to the first 6.5 d of the 14 longer cycles (LBE batch 1, LBE batch 3) misses their final yield by a median -42% although the nominal potential SE is small (median 2.4% on full cycles): 7-day cycles do not identify the asymptote and the Jacobian SE is overconfident. Median |corr(potential, rate)| 0.66; 17% of fits hit a bound.
182 of 348 cycles are excluded by conflicts, carry-over, co-interventions or ambiguous labels.
13 of 14 chemistry units are unresolved; methane units are builder-asserted; only LBE applies a volume correction; TS/VS bases differ between labs.
18 admitted bottles in 7 arms, 2 labs, 1 biochar material and 0 committed descriptors, against 2928 time rows; the smallest attainable exact two-sided p for any contrast is 0.10.
Sanglier is repeated batch with recirculation; no continuous-reactor methane data with matched biochar dosing are in the repository to test transfer.

Source records contradict three convenient assumptions: labels 1/2 are not one dose across labs (4/8 g vs 2.5/5 g initial biochar); FAN is derived from TAN and pH, not measured; the ammonium event's single-condition scope disagrees with Inoculation grams for every BRL bottle.
